title: Add E2E tests for #incidents interactions (timeouts + degraded mode)
author: Devon Price
description: Context: Incident Bot v2 adds richer context cards and more interactive actions, but the reliability bar for #incidents is higher than our existing unit/integration coverage. This PR adds an end-to-end test harness that exercises the Slack flow we care about in production: message in #incidents -> bot posts context cards -> user clicks "Refresh" / "Expand" -> bot acks within Slack deadlines and updates blocks. Scope: (1) basic happy-path for a new incident thread, (2) upstream timeouts (deploy metadata + telemetry) and the expected user-facing degraded-mode behavior (cached context + deep links + "try again" action), and (3) idempotency for repeated interactive actions (double-click, retry delivery). Non-goals: This does not add new bot features; it focuses on validating existing behavior introduced in pr-1860 and pr-1865 and preventing regressions as we tune timeouts/caching. Implementation details: Uses a lightweight local "Slack API" simulator (events + interactive payloads) plus a fake upstream dependency server (deploy/config/telemetry) with controllable delay/error injection; assertions are against the rendered Block Kit payload (sanitized snapshot) and the timing of acks/updates. Tests are designed to be deterministic in CI (no real Slack tokens; signature validation uses test keys; clocks are faked for timeout paths).
commits: test(e2e): add incidents channel harness + slack simulator
test(e2e): cover timeout -> degraded mode rendering + deep links
test(e2e): enforce ack deadline + idempotent action handling
ci: wire e2e suite into buildkite with quarantined retries
chore: refactor block rendering helpers for snapshot stability
conversation: Miles Thornton (reviewer): Love that we're finally asserting the #incidents UX end-to-end. Two questions: (1) are we actually validating ack timing, or just that we call ack() at some point? (2) the degraded-mode snapshot includes raw error strings from upstream; we should ensure we don't leak internal hostnames in user-visible blocks. Also please link the degraded-mode behavior to the runbook language from ENG-5429.

Devon Price (author): (1) Yes: the simulator records timestamps for the interactive request + when our handler calls ack(); test fails if > 2500ms. I picked 2500ms to give headroom under CI jitter while still catching regressions (Slack hard limit is 3000ms). (2) Good call. I updated the degraded-mode renderer to map upstream errors to a small set of user-safe reasons (timeout/unavailable/permission) and moved internal details to debug logs only. Added a snapshot assertion that there are no URLs except console deep links.

Jacob Stein (reviewer): For the timeout case, can we also cover "partial" degraded mode where deploy context succeeds but telemetry times out? That was the real-world pattern from INT-3341; we still want to show deploys + a smaller telemetry section with links.

Devon Price (author): Added a new test case "telemetry timeout only". The fake upstream server now allows per-endpoint delays; snapshot shows Recent deploys populated, Saturation signals replaced with cached/links, and the footer includes a single "Retry telemetry" button.

Allison Grant (reviewer): Snapshot stability: the dashboard links include a time window using Date.now(). Can we pin the clock so snapshots don't churn? Also please ensure link params match the incident-context guidelines (service, region, lookback).

Devon Price (author): Updated the e2e harness to use fake timers + fixed epoch and injected "incident started at". Link generator now takes explicit start/end; tests assert the query params include service, region, and 30m lookback. Snapshot is stable now.

Dylan Brooks (reviewer): CI: I'm worried about e2e tests being flaky. Can we keep them on main pipeline but add limited retry + better failure artifacts? We should also avoid parallel port collisions.

Devon Price (author): Added buildkite step with 1 retry on infra failures, uploads the simulator logs + rendered blocks as artifacts, and uses dynamic port allocation. Also changed the harness to run serially to avoid shared state issues.
Miles Thornton (reviewer): Requested changes addressed. Approving. Please add a short README section so future changes know how to run the harness locally.
Devon Price (author): Added README: `pnpm test:e2e:incidents` and notes on controlling upstream delays via env vars.
release_notes: Internal-only: Add E2E coverage for #incidents Slack interactions, including timeout and degraded-mode behavior.
